descriptionChirho: The cupped hollow of the hand or fist, always in dual form (chophnayim), denoting the two hands together as a unit for grasping, holding, or scooping; used for handfuls of soot (Exod 9:8), incense (Lev 16:12), wind or toil (Eccl 4:6), and as a measure of God's creative power (Prov 30:4; Ezek 10:2, 7).
